posts.text: Originally called Decoration Day, Black Americans interred the bodies of fallen Union soldiers to honor their sacrifice — now known as Memorial Day. Decades later, my great-grandfather served our nation in WWI. Then my grandfather took post in WWII and the Korean War. Today and every day, I honor their sacrifice by fighting for rights they were denied in a country they loved, knowing freedom will prevail if we refuse to give up the battle.

This weekend, I joined the @uwomenfaith Assembly in Indianapolis, where I had the honor of meeting Elizabeth Eckford. One of the Little Rock Nine, she bravely integrated an all-white high school in 1957. Her courage advanced the civil rights movement, but almost 70 years later, we find ourselves continuing to fight for equality. Because our freedom is never free — but it is ours to win.

Photo by Mike DuBose, United Women in Faith.

Children and families are being held in ICE detention facilities across the country right now. It is wrong, it is immoral, and it will be a stain on the American consciousness for a generation. That's why we're gathering in Washington, D.C. today with @NDWA to demand an end to family and child detention. #ReadThemHome
